name: Non-cash payment fraud Directive
evidence_rating: thin: only a legal transposition report; fraud statistics exist but no study links them to the Directive; impact evaluation (due May 2026) not found
summary: The Directive updated criminal law on payment card and online payment fraud. The Commission's only review so far checked legal transposition, finding most countries late and some gaps on virtual currencies. Payment fraud in Europe still runs at about EUR 4 billion a year, but no study has assessed whether the Directive helped reduce it.

indicators.objective: The proposal's financial statement has no indicators section; Article 18 required a monitoring programme (set out in SWD(2023) 23) and Article 21 a transposition report (2023) and an impact evaluation by 31 May 2026

indicators.indicator: Clear, robust, technology-neutral criminal law framework (incl. virtual currencies, stolen credentials)
indicators.evidence: Transposition report: 9 Member States on time; infringement cases opened against 16 in July 2021; most provisions transposed, with gaps notably on virtual currency coverage.

indicators.indicator: Eliminate operational obstacles to cross-border investigation and prosecution
indicators.evidence: No outcome data published; the impact evaluation due May 2026 was not found.

indicators.indicator: Reduce direct losses from non-cash payment fraud and raise trust
indicators.evidence: Fraud is tracked by the ECB/EBA under PSD2 reporting (EUR 4.3bn in 2022, EUR 2.0bn in H1 2023 across instruments), but these figures cannot be attributed to the Directive.

indicators.indicator: One-off EUR 561,000 and about EUR 2.3m a year across Member States

literature.citation: European Commission (2017), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal on combating fraud and counterfeiting of non-cash means of payment (executive summary SWD(2017) 299), SWD(2017) 298
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal on combating fraud and counterfeiting of non-cash means of payment (executive summary SWD(2017) 299)
literature.outcomes: law enforcement effectiveness; costs to Member States
literature.headline: Expected more effective law enforcement, better cross-border and public-private cooperation and more trust in the digital single market; costs EUR 561,000 one-off and about EUR 2.3m a year for Member States; no impact on SMEs
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected the update of criminal law on payment fraud to make police work more effective at a modest cost to national authorities, but gave no forecast of reduced fraud.

literature.citation: European Commission (2023), Report assessing the extent to which Member States have taken the necessary measures to comply with Directive (EU) 2019/713, COM(2023) 363
literature.title: Report assessing the extent to which Member States have taken the necessary measures to comply with Directive (EU) 2019/713
literature.headline: Only 9 Member States transposed on time; infringement procedures against 16 in July 2021; transposition largely complete by 2023 but gaps remain, notably on coverage of virtual currencies
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's check found most countries transposed the payment-fraud rules late but largely correctly, with gaps on virtual currencies.
literature.quality: legal compliance only; no impact data

literature.citation: European Banking Authority & European Central Bank (2024), 2024 Report on Payment Fraud, EBA/ECB joint report (1 August 2024)
literature.authors: European Banking Authority & European Central Bank
literature.title: 2024 Report on Payment Fraud
literature.headline: Payment fraud in the EEA totalled EUR 4.3bn in 2022 and EUR 2.0bn in H1 2023; card fraud about 0.031% of card payment value, mostly in remote transactions
literature.summary_plain: European regulators' statistics show payment fraud of about EUR 4 billion a year, mostly online, but they do not show whether this Directive made a difference.
literature.quality: descriptive; no link to the Directive

literature.authors: European Banking Authority & European Central Bank
literature.title: 2025 Report on Payment Fraud
literature.method: descriptive statistics on semi-annual PSP fraud reporting (PSD2 Art. 96(6) and ECB payment statistics), EEA, 2022-2024
literature.outcomes: value and rate of payment fraud by instrument; SCA effectiveness
literature.headline: EEA payment fraud rose from EUR 3.4bn (2022) and EUR 3.5bn (2023) to EUR 4.2bn (2024), stable at about 0.002% of transaction value; credit-transfer losses EUR 2.2bn (+16%) and card losses EUR 1.33bn (+29%).
literature.summary_plain: Official figures on how much payment fraud happens in Europe. Totals are rising, especially scams where people are tricked into sending money, even though fraud remains a tiny share of all payments.
literature.quality: Authoritative outcome monitoring for the Directive's target, but not attributable to the Directive (effects mainly linked to PSD2 SCA); press release read
literature.citation: European Banking Authority & European Central Bank (2025), 2025 Report on Payment Fraud, EBA-ECB joint report, 15 December 2025

literature.title: Report on card fraud in 2020 and 2021
literature.method: descriptive statistics from 20 card payment scheme operators, SEPA-issued cards
literature.outcomes: card fraud value and rate; card-not-present and cross-border fraud
literature.headline: Card fraud fell to 0.028% of card payment value in 2021 (EUR 1.53bn of EUR 5.40trn, vs EUR 1.87bn in 2019), with card-not-present fraud down 12% from 2020; cross-border transactions were 11% of value but 63% of fraud.
literature.summary_plain: Card fraud in Europe hit a record low in 2021, around when the Directive had to be transposed, mostly thanks to stronger online payment checks.
literature.quality: Outcome trend spanning the May 2021 transposition deadline; decline attributed by ECB to PSD2 SCA, not the Directive; press release read
literature.citation: European Central Bank (2023), Report on card fraud in 2020 and 2021, ECB report, 26 May 2023
